samples.summary: New backend alignment allowlist has no positive test for any legal value
samples.evidence: The new validator `assertValidBlockStyle` gates `style.alignment` on `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS = {left,center,right,justify}` (docs-content.controller.ts:254). The two new tests only cover (a) a hostile string being rejected and (b) `style: {}` with no alignment at all — the latter passed identically before this change, since alignment was never validated. No test PUTs `alignment: 'center'`/'justify'/'right'/'left', so if a member were dropped from or mistyped in the set, legitimate documents would start getting 400s and the suite would stay green. Also untested: the nested path (a bad alignment on a block inside `tableData.rows[].cells[].blocks[]`), even though `assertValidBlock` recurses there.
searchedFor: read the whole 'docs block shape validation' describe block (lines 398-524)

samples.summary: buildParagraphPropertiesXml's new default branch (unknown/undefined alignment) is only tested with a hostile string
samples.evidence: The change replaces `style.alignment === 'justify' ? 'both' : style.alignment` with `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[...] ?? 'left'`. That silently changes the `alignment === undefined` case: previously it emitted `<w:jc w:val="undefined"/>` (since `undefined !== 'left'`), now it emits nothing. `grep -n 'w:jc' packages/docs` shows the only export-side assertions are 'center', 'justify'→'both' and the new hostile-string case; there is no test for `alignment: undefined` (nor for 'left' emitting nothing, nor 'right'). The behavioral difference the map introduces at the default branch is therefore unasserted.

samples.summary: PPTX bullet-marker color (buClr) path changed but only run-level colors are tested
samples.evidence: `markerToXml` was changed from `if (marker.color != null)` to `const buClr = storedColorToThemeColor(marker.color); if (buClr)`, so a marker color of `''`, `{kind:'srgb',value:''}`, `rgb(...)` or a hostile string now behaves differently. The new tests in packages/slides/test/export/pptx/text.test.ts only build runs via `para('X', {color/backgroundColor/underlineColor})`; grep for `buClr` in packages/slides/test shows only import-side tests and a round-trip fixture with a valid hex (`FF9900`/`FF0000`). No export test exercises a cleared or CSS marker color, so the normalization at that sink (including a normalized `rgb()` → `val="RRGGBB"`) is unverified even though the plan doc claims marker coverage.

samples.summary: removedCellStyleAttrs covers 7 cell-style keys; only backgroundColor is tested
samples.evidence: The new helper returns removal attribute names for backgroundColor, verticalAlign, padding and the four borders, and the only new test ('should clear the fill in the CRDT when backgroundColor is undefined', yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2033) exercises backgroundColor. The border keys serialize as composite strings (`serializeCellStyle` lines 241-244) so a name mismatch there would be silent; nothing asserts that clearing e.g. `borderTop: undefined` or `padding: undefined` actually removes the attribute from the Tree node.

samples.summary: Reset assertion cannot distinguish an explicitly-undefined key from an absent key — the exact distinction the fix depends on
samples.evidence: `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` uses jest/vitest recursive equality, under which `{}` equals `{color: undefined}`. The store's removal logic is `key in style && style[key] === undefined` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:147, and the new removedCellStyleAttrs at 260), i.e. it needs the KEY PRESENT. A future refactor that stripped the key before calling `applyStyle` would break the clear-in-CRDT behavior while this test stayed green. An `Object.keys(...)`/`toHaveProperty('color')` style assertion would close it. (The test does still catch the original `""` regression.)

samples.summary: Two of the three changed reset call sites have no test
samples.evidence: The new color-reset.test.ts renders only `TextFormatGroup`. The identical reset change in `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx` (slim/mobile docs toolbar, lines 490 and 512 → `handleTextColor(undefined)` / `handleHighlightColor(undefined)`) and the cell 'No fill' change in `docs-table-context-menu.tsx` (line 230 → `applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: undefined })`) are untested at the component level, so either could regress back to `""` without a failing test. Searched packages/frontend/tests for any render of DocsFormattingToolbar / DocsTableContextMenu and found none.
